a1.01: Hi. I'm really glad you're here. This first walk is five minutes, and we'll do it sitting down.
a1.02: Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat, hands resting on your thighs.
a1.03: Your phone can stay in your pocket. If anything hurts, just stop. There's no wrong way to do this.
a1.04: Let's begin with heel taps. Lift your heels, then set them down.
a1.05: If that feels fine, lift your whole foot a little. One side, then the other. That's marching.
a1.06: Let your arms swing gently, like you're walking out to the mailbox.
a1.07: Nice and easy. Breathe in through your nose… and out through your mouth.
a1.08: Sit tall, like a string is lifting the top of your head.
a1.09: If you'd like a little more, lift your knees a bit higher. Only if it feels good.
a1.10: You're doing it. This is your time.
a1.11: Keep that steady rhythm. You should be able to talk, or even hum along.
a1.12: In a few seconds, we'll pick up the pace, just a little.
a1.13: A little quicker now. Same small steps, just a bit faster.
a1.14: Still able to talk? Good. That's the right pace for you.
a1.16: And slow it down. Easy marching, nice and relaxed.
a1.17: Shake out your hands if you like. Keep your feet moving gently.
a1.18: One more quicker round coming up. Just thirty seconds.
a1.19: Quicker again. If heel taps feel better right now, that's perfect.
a1.20: Want a little more? Let your arms swing a bit bigger.
a1.22: And ease off. Slow, comfortable steps.
a1.23: Notice how your legs feel right now. Maybe a little warmer.
a1.25: Slow your feet until they rest flat on the floor.
a1.26: Roll your shoulders back, slowly. Two or three times.
a1.27: Take a deep breath in… and let it go.
a1.28: One more breath in… and out.
a1.29: That's five minutes. You showed up today, and that's the hardest part.
a1.30: Your first walk took you to Central Park Zoo. When you're ready, take a look. There's a postcard waiting for you.
a2.open.1: Welcome back. Let's get your feet moving.
a2.open.2: Good to see you. This walk is all at your pace.
a2.open.3: Ready when you are. Let's start slow and easy.
a2.open.4: Here we go. Easy steps first, and we'll build from there.
a2.setup.seated.1: Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat, back tall.
a2.setup.seated.2: Find the front of your seat and plant your feet. Hands can rest on your thighs.
a2.setup.seated.3: Use a sturdy chair with no wheels. Sit tall, away from the back.
a2.setup.seated.joint: A higher chair works best for you, with arms if you have one.
a2.setup.inplace.1: Stand near your chair so you can hold it if you need to. Feet about hip-width apart.
a2.setup.inplace.2: Stand tall with your chair close by. Soft knees, relaxed shoulders.
a2.setup.inplace.3: Clear a little space around you. Keep your chair on your left, within reach.
a2.setup.inplace.shoes: Shoes with good grip are best. Please skip socks on a smooth floor.
a2.setup.pad.1: Hold on, and step onto the belt while it moves slowly.
a2.setup.pad.2: Start your pad nice and slow. You can change the speed anytime.
a2.pad.moves: On the pad, we just walk and use our arms. No side steps on the belt.
a2.warm.1: Easy steps to start. Let your arms swing naturally.
a2.warm.2: Keep it light. Heels, then toes, nice and steady.
a2.warm.3: Roll your shoulders once or twice. Stay loose.
a2.warm.4: Just warming up. No rush at all.
a2.warm.5: Look ahead, not down at your feet.
a2.warm.6: Stand tall, like a string is lifting the top of your head.
a2.warm.7: Breathe easy. Your breath should stay calm here.
a2.warm.8: Soft knees, relaxed hands. Let each step land gently.
a2.soon.1: Quicker steps coming up in a few seconds.
a2.soon.2: Get ready to pick up the pace, just a little.
a2.soon.3: Ten seconds, then a little quicker.
a2.soon.4: In ten seconds, we'll go a little faster. Same move.
a2.next.1: Nearly time for something new. Ten more seconds.
a2.now.1: Now let's do it together, right side first.
a2.now.2: Your turn. Join in whenever you're ready.
a2.now.3: Together now. Nice and easy to start.
a2.move.march.demo: The right knee lifts, the foot sets down, then the left.
a2.move.march.seated: Sit tall. Lift each foot a little off the floor, and set it down flat.
a2.move.march.inplace: Stand tall. Each foot lands softly, heel first, then the toes.
a2.move.march.easy: For an easier version, just lift your heels. Toes stay on the floor.
a2.move.march.harder: For a little more, lift your knees higher, but keep them below your hips.
a2.move.march.joint: Keep your knees well below your hips the whole time.
a2.move.march.next: Ten more seconds. Next up: March.
a2.move.heel-dig.intro: Heel dig. Heel out in front, toes up.
a2.move.heel-dig.demo: The right heel reaches forward, toes point up, then it comes back.
a2.move.heel-dig.seated: Slide your foot forward, rest the heel down, and pull your toes toward you.
a2.move.heel-dig.inplace: Keep your standing knee soft, and your chair within reach.
a2.move.heel-dig.easy: For an easier version, go slower, and keep the heel close to you.
a2.move.heel-dig.harder: For a little more, switch feet a little quicker, in a steady rhythm.
a2.move.heel-dig.next: Ten more seconds. Next up: Heel dig.
a2.move.side-step.demo.seated: The right foot steps out to the side, then back in.
a2.move.side-step.demo.inplace: Step to the right, and bring your left foot to meet it.
a2.move.side-step.seated: Keep your foot low as it slides out. Your hips stay still on the seat.
a2.move.side-step.inplace: Two steps to the right, then two back to the left. Hips level, knees soft.
a2.move.side-step.easy: For an easier version, take smaller steps, with your hands on your hips.
a2.move.side-step.harder: For a little more, take wider steps and open your arms out to the sides.
a2.move.side-step.dizzy: Keep your steps small, and stay close to your chair.
a2.move.side-step.next: Ten more seconds. Next up: Side step.
a2.move.knee-lift.intro: Knee lift. A little higher than a march.
a2.move.knee-lift.demo: The right knee comes up, foot pointing forward, then down.
a2.move.knee-lift.seated: Hold the sides of your seat if you like. Sit tall as you lift.
a2.move.knee-lift.inplace: Rest your left hand on your chair. Your knee comes no higher than your hip.
a2.move.knee-lift.easy: For an easier version, lift just a little, and hold your chair.
a2.move.knee-lift.harder: For a little more, touch each knee with the opposite hand.
a2.move.knee-lift.joint: Keep your knee clearly below your hip. A lower lift is just right.
a2.move.knee-lift.next: Ten more seconds. Next up: Knee lift.
a2.move.toe-tap.demo: The right toes tap the floor in front, then come back.
a2.move.toe-tap.seated: Reach your foot a little forward, tap, and bring it home under your knee.
a2.move.toe-tap.inplace: Keep your standing knee soft, and stay tall. Don't lean back.
a2.move.toe-tap.easy: For an easier version, tap a little closer to you, and slower.
a2.move.toe-tap.harder: For a little more, turn the tap into a low kick. Keep that knee a little bent.
a2.move.toe-tap.knees: Keep it a gentle tap today. No kicks.
a2.move.toe-tap.next: Ten more seconds. Next up: Toe tap forward.
a2.move.heel-back.demo.seated: The right heel slides back under your chair, then forward again.
a2.move.heel-back.demo.inplace: The right heel comes back and up behind you, then sets down.
a2.move.heel-back.seated: Sit tall, feet flat. Slide one heel back, then the other.
a2.move.heel-back.inplace: Stand behind your chair, both hands on the back. Stay tall, no leaning forward.
a2.move.heel-back.easy: For an easier version, make it smaller. Halfway up is plenty.
a2.move.heel-back.harder: For a little more, let go of the chair if you feel steady. Stay close to it.
a2.move.heel-back.joint: Bend your knee only as far as feels comfortable.
a2.move.heel-back.next: Ten more seconds. Next up: Heel to back.
a2.move.shift.demo.seated: Lean gently to the right, then through the middle to the left.
a2.move.shift.demo.inplace: Shift your weight onto your right foot, then over to the left.
a2.move.shift.seated: Keep both feet flat and your head level. Just a small lean.
a2.move.shift.inplace: Feet a little wider than your hips. Knees point the same way as your toes.
a2.move.shift.easy: For an easier version, hold your chair, and keep the shift small.
a2.move.shift.harder: For a little more, let the lighter heel lift a little off the floor.
a2.move.shift.next: Ten more seconds. Next up: Weight shift.
a2.move.arms.swing: Arm swing. Bend your elbows, and swing your arms with your steps.
a2.move.arms.press: Arm press. Push your hands forward at shoulder height, then draw them back.
a2.move.arms.soft: Keep your elbows soft, never locked straight.
a2.move.arms.easy: For an easier version, keep your hands below your shoulders.
a2.move.arms.harder: For a little more, press up and out at an angle, if your shoulders feel good.
a2.move.arms.shoulders: Keep your arms below shoulder height today. Small and easy is fine.
a2.move.arms.pad: If you feel steady, let go and swing your arms. Keep the rail close.
a2.move.arms.next: Ten more seconds. Next up: Arm swing.
a2.brisk.seated.1: A little quicker now. March your feet, and let your arms join in.
a2.brisk.seated.2: Pick up the pace in your chair. Quick, small steps.
a2.brisk.seated.3: A little faster arms now. Your feet can follow.
a2.brisk.seated.4: A little quicker, same move. Swing your arms a bit bigger.
a2.brisk.inplace.1: A little quicker now. Lift your knees a bit and swing your arms.
a2.brisk.inplace.2: Pick up the pace, right where you are. Stay close to your chair.
a2.brisk.inplace.3: Quicker steps now, same move. Let your arms help.
a2.brisk.inplace.4: A little faster now. Keep your steps small and light.
a2.brisk.pad.1: Turn your pad up a notch, or just take quicker steps.
a2.brisk.pad.2: A little faster now, if it feels right. Hold the rail, or your table, as you speed up.
a2.brisk.pad.3: Same speed is fine too. Just swing your arms a bit more.
a2.brisk.again.1: Here we go again. Quicker steps.
a2.brisk.again.2: Brisk again. Find that same rhythm.
a2.brisk.again.3: And a little quicker again. Same move.
a2.brisk.again.4: Back to a little quicker. Your arms can do some of the work.
a2.brisk.mid.1: You should be breathing a bit harder, but still able to talk.
a2.brisk.mid.2: Nice rhythm. Keep your shoulders relaxed.
a2.brisk.mid.3: If it feels like too much, slow down a little. That still counts.
a2.brisk.mid.4: Look ahead, and keep breathing. You're doing well.
a2.brisk.last: Last quicker round. You've got this.
a2.brisk.end.1: Ten more seconds, then we slow down.
a2.brisk.end.2: Almost done with the quicker part. Ten more seconds.
a2.talk.1: Quick check. You can still talk, but singing would be hard. That's the spot.
a2.talk.2: Try saying a few words out loud. If that's easy, you're doing fine.
a2.talk.3: Hard to get the words out? Slow down until talking feels easy.
a2.talk.seated: You should be able to chat easily. Add a little more arm swing if you like.
a2.easy.1: And ease off. Easy steps, catch your breath.
a2.easy.2: Slow it down. Nice and relaxed.
a2.easy.3: Back to easy. Same move, a little slower.
a2.easy.4: Nice and easy again. Let your arms relax.
a2.easy.mid.1: Let your breathing settle. You're doing well.
a2.easy.mid.3: Easy pace. This part matters just as much.
a2.round.1: Another quicker round in a few seconds.
a2.round.2: Get ready. One more round coming up.
a2.gentle.1: Steady and easy. There's nothing to hurry today.
a2.gentle.2: Keep this gentle pace. Moving is what matters.
a2.gentle.3: Stay comfortable. Smaller is fine, too.
a2.gentle.arms: If you'd like a little more, bring your arms in.
a2.cool.seated.1: Time to wind down. Slow your feet until they're barely moving.
a2.cool.seated.2: Let's slow down. Small, easy steps in your chair.
a2.cool.inplace.1: Time to wind down. Slow, gentle steps, then let your feet rest.
a2.cool.inplace.2: Slow march now. Arms low and loose.
a2.cool.pad.1: Bring your pad down to a slow stroll.
a2.cool.pad.2: Hold on as you step off. Then stand behind your chair.
a2.cool.mid.1: Shake out your hands. Let your breathing slow down.
a2.cool.mid.2: Nice and slow. Let your breathing come back to easy.
a2.cool.mid.3: Notice your breath slowing down. You did the work.
a2.cool.feet: Let your feet come to rest.
a2.cool.stretch.1: Now, a few easy stretches to finish.
a2.cool.stretch.2: Let's finish with two gentle stretches. Stay right where you are.
a2.cool.breath.last: And one last breath in… and slowly out.
a2.close.1: That's your walk for today. Well done.
a2.close.2: All done. Every minute counts, and you did them all.
a2.close.3: That's it for today. Your journey just moved a little further.
a2.close.4: That's your walk. Thank you for making time for yourself.
a2.close.5: Walk done. Have a sip of water when you can.
a2.close.6: Lovely work. Enjoy the rest of your day.
a2.long.open: A longer walk today, with plenty of easy time built in.
a2.long.round.2: Round two. Same easy start, then a little quicker.
a2.long.round.3: Last round. Take it at your pace.
a2.long.half: About halfway. Have a sip of water, if you have some nearby.
a2.long.tired: Feeling tired? Stay at the easy pace from here. It all counts.
a3.open.1: Let's head out. Start with an easy stroll.
a3.open.2: Out the door we go. Nice and easy for the first couple of minutes.
a3.safe.1: Keep one ear free so you can hear what's around you.
a3.safe.2: Pick up the pace a little. Keep an eye out for curbs.
a3.safe.3: Quicker steps, but watch the ground ahead.
a3.safe.4: If it's warm, look for shade, and take a sip of water.
a3.brisk.1: A little quicker now. Swing your arms and walk tall.
a3.easy.1: Ease back to a comfortable stroll.
a3.break.1: Find somewhere to sit or lean, in the shade if you can.
a3.home.1: Let's walk home gently. Easy pace from here.
a3.cool.1: Slow down to an easy stroll to finish.
a3.close.1: Lovely walk. When you're home, your chair moves are waiting, if you'd like them.
a5.rest20: Rest for twenty seconds. Sip some water if you like.
a6.2: Nice and steady. That's exactly right.
a6.3: Your pace is the right pace.
a6.5: Look at you, keeping it going.
a6.6: That's a little stronger than last time.
a6.7: Take it easy on yourself. You showed up.
a7.break.1: Take your time. Sit down, sip some water, and breathe slowly.
a7.break.2: Whenever you're ready. There's no hurry.
a7.resume: Welcome back. Let's ease back in, nice and slow.
a7.finish: That's a good place to stop. Today still counts.
a7.hurt.easier: Here's an easier version. Go gently.
a7.hurt.skip: We'll skip that one. On to the next.
a7.hurt.stop: Let's stop here. Rest up, and we'll adjust your plan.
a7.stand: Stand behind your chair. Hold on if you need to.
a7.stand.wait: We'll start in ten seconds. Tap Wait if you need longer.
a7.stand.ready: Hold the chair the whole time. Only let go if you feel steady.
a7.pause: Paused. Take all the time you need.
a7.dizzy: If you feel dizzy or unwell, stop and sit down.
a8.ny.1: You've reached Central Park Zoo. Your journey through New York starts here.
a8.ny.2: You've made it to Bethesda Fountain, right in the heart of the park.
a8.ny.3: Welcome to Times Square. Bright lights, and you walked here.
a8.ny.4: Bryant Park. A green, quiet corner in the middle of the city.
a8.ny.5: You've arrived at Union Square. Just a little further to the bridge.
a8.ny.6: You made it to the Brooklyn Bridge. That's the whole of New York. Well done.
a8.smoky.1: Welcome to Cades Cove, a quiet valley in the Smoky Mountains.
a8.camino.1: You're in Sarria, where the last stretch of the Camino begins.
a8.ne.1: Portland Head Light, standing tall on the coast of Maine.
a8.pch.1: Carmel-by-the-Sea. Your walk along the Pacific coast begins.
a9.to-chair: Nice walking. Now a few chair moves.
a9.to-stretch: Let's finish with a gentle stretch.
a9.chair.open: Chair moves today. Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat.
a9.chair.close: That's all your moves for today. Nicely done.
a9.gentle: Your joints are a bit achy today, so we'll keep it gentle.
a9.strong: Feeling good today? Let's make the most of it, at your pace.
a9.back.1: Welcome back. Your journey is right where you left it.
a9.back.2: Good to have you back. Let's start with an easy five minutes.
a9.shorter: We made today a little shorter. Build up at your pace.
a9.levelup: You're ready for a little more. Today we'll try the next level.
a9.leveldown: We'll keep things seated for now. That's a smart choice.
a9.extras: A little extra today. Just a few minutes.
a5.10s.change: Ten more seconds, then we change.
a5.10s.rest: Ten more seconds, then a short rest.
a5.last.2: And the last one. Nice and slow.
a7.pad.start: Stand with your feet on the sides of your pad, then start the belt.
a7.pad.slow: Start at the slowest speed. Build up a little at a time.
a7.pad.rail: Hold the rail if your pad has one, or rest a hand on a sturdy table.
a7.pad.clip: If your pad has a safety clip, clip it to your clothes.
a7.pad.phone: Leave your phone on the table. Just follow the voice.
a7.pad.off: Stop the belt first. Wait until it's still, then step off.
a7.pad.dizzy: Feeling dizzy? Stop the belt, hold on, then sit down.
a7.morning.1: Sit tall for three breaths. If you feel dizzy, stay seated.
a7.morning.2: Stand up slowly, then stay still for one breath before you move.
a7.stop.1: If you feel sharp pain, chest pain, or dizziness, stop and rest.
a7.stop.2: If it keeps happening, talk to your doctor.
a7.stop.breath: If you can't catch your breath, slow down or stop.
a4.warm.1: Let's warm up in your chair first. An easy march to start.
a4.warm.toe: Now toe taps. Heels stay down, lift your toes and tap them.
a4.warm.done: Nice and warm. Let's start the moves.
a4.demo.2: Just watch this first one. No need to move yet.
a4.demo.3: Watch me do one, nice and slow.
a4.with-me.2: Your turn. Let's do it together.
a4.with-me.3: Now with me, at your own pace.
a4.breath.1: Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.
a4.breath.2: Keep breathing. Never hold your breath.
a4.slow.1: Slow on the way down. No dropping.
a4.slow.2: Smooth and steady. Slower is better here.
a4.count.stop: Stop while you could still do two more. That's the right effort.
a4.pain.2: If it hurts, make it smaller or skip it.
a4.range: Move only as far as feels comfortable.
a4.rest.2: Let your arms and legs relax. Breathe in… and out.
a4.rest.3: Shake out your hands. Next move in a moment.
a4.stand.setup: Stand behind your chair, both hands on the chair back.
a4.stand.chair: Use a sturdy chair that won't slide. A kitchen counter works too.
a4.to-stand.1: Hands on the chair, take a breath, then stand.
a4.to-stand.2: Stand still for a breath before we start.
a4.to-stand.sts: After this last one, stay standing.
a4.to-stand.behind: Now step behind your chair and hold on with both hands.
a4.to-sit.1: Walk around to the front of your chair. Take your time.
a4.to-sit.2: Reach back for the seat, and sit down slowly.
a4.rotate.1: A few different moves today, to keep things fresh.
a4.rotate.2: This one is new. We'll take it slow.
a4.v1.1: Sit-to-stand. It helps with getting up from any chair.
a4.v1.2: Scoot to the front of your chair. Feet flat, about hip-width apart.
a4.v1.3: If you need help, put your hands on the chair and push. That's a great way to start.
a4.v1.4: Lean forward, nose over toes… and stand up.
a4.v1.5: Now sit back down, slowly. Reach back for the chair with your hips.
a4.v1.6: Take a breath whenever you need one.
a4.v1.7: Want more? Cross your arms over your chest, and sit down on a slow count of three.
a4.v1.breath: Breathe out as you stand, breathe in as you sit.
a4.v1.top: Stand all the way up, and take one full breath.
a4.v1.var.joint: Use a higher chair today, with arms if you have one.
a4.v1.var.joint-lean: Keep your chest up, lean only a little… and stand up.
a4.v2.1: Seated knee lift. The same move you use for every step.
a4.v2.2: Hold the sides of your seat lightly. Sit tall.
a4.v2.3: Start small. Just lift your heel, then set it down.
a4.v2.4: If that feels fine, lift your whole knee a little. Then switch sides.
a4.v2.5: Keep your back tall. No need to lean back.
a4.v2.6: Want more? Lift a little higher and swing the opposite arm.
a4.v2.7: Nice and steady. Ten more seconds.
a4.v2.var.joint: Keep your knee lower than your hip. A small lift is plenty.
a4.v3.1: Seated leg extension. The move you use for climbing stairs.
a4.v3.2: Sit tall and hold the sides of your seat.
a4.v3.3: Start with a small lift. Straighten your leg just halfway.
a4.v3.4: If that's comfortable, straighten it more, toes to the ceiling. Keep the knee soft.
a4.v3.5: Keep your leg pointing straight ahead… and lower it slowly.
a4.v3.6: Want more? Hold it up for a count of three.
a4.v3.7: If your knee complains, make the lift smaller. That still counts.
a4.v3.breath: Breathe out as you straighten, breathe in as you lower.
a4.v4.1: Heel and toe raises. The move you use for reaching a high shelf.
a4.v4.2: Sit tall, feet flat on the floor.
a4.v4.3: Lift your heels a little, then lower them.
a4.v4.4: Now the other way. Lift your toes, heels stay down.
a4.v4.6: Want more? Stand behind your chair, hold on with both hands, and rise onto your toes.
a4.v4.var.dizzy: Let's keep this one seated today.
a4.v5.1: Wall push-up. It makes pushing doors and lifting bags easier.
a4.v5.2: Stand about an arm's length from the wall. Hands flat, at shoulder height.
a4.v5.3: Start by standing a little closer. Bend your elbows just a bit.
a4.v5.4: Bring your chest toward the wall… and press back.
a4.v5.5: Keep your body straight, like a plank of wood.
a4.v5.6: Want more? Step your feet back a little.
a4.v5.breath: Breathe in as you lean in, breathe out as you press back.
a4.v5.heels: Heels stay on the floor. Arms straight at the end, not locked.
a4.v5.var.shoulder: Keep it small. Bend your elbows only a little, then press back.
a4.v6.1: Single-leg stand. Stand behind your chair and hold on with both hands.
a4.v6.2: Start easy. Lift just your heel, toes stay down.
a4.v6.3: If you feel steady, lift your foot a little off the floor.
a4.v6.4: Look at one spot in front of you. It helps.
a4.v6.5: Hold… you're doing great… and set it down.
a4.v6.6: If you wobble, that's normal. Hold the chair a little tighter.
a4.v6.7: Want more? Try holding on with just one hand.
a4.v6.var.dizzy: Keep both hands on the chair the whole time.
a4.v6.breath: Keep breathing slowly while you hold.
a4.side-leg.intro: Side leg raise. For stepping sideways and getting in and out of the car.
a4.side-leg.setup.1: Feet close together, toes pointing forward.
a4.side-leg.demo.1: The leg lifts out to the side, foot about as high as your other shin.
a4.side-leg.breath: Breathe out as your leg goes out, breathe in as it comes back.
a4.side-leg.easier: Easier: lift it just a little. A small lift still counts.
a4.side-leg.form.1: Keep your toes facing forward, not up to the ceiling.
a4.side-leg.form.2: Stand tall. Don't lean away from the leg.
a4.side-leg.harder: Want more? Hold the chair with just one hand.
a4.side-leg.var.joint: Keep it small, with your toes pointing forward the whole time.
a4.side-leg.done: Set your foot down softly. Both sides done.
a4.back-leg.intro: Back leg raise. For stronger steps, like walking up a hill.
a4.back-leg.setup.1: Stand close to your chair, feet hip-width apart.
a4.back-leg.demo.1: The leg moves straight back, just a little. The leg stays long.
a4.back-leg.breath: Breathe out as your leg goes back, breathe in as it returns.
a4.back-leg.easier: Easier: a smaller lift. Just a little way back.
a4.back-leg.form.1: Stand tall. Don't lean forward or arch your back.
a4.back-leg.form.2: Toes point down toward the floor.
a4.back-leg.harder: Want more? Hold it at the top a little longer.
a4.back-leg.var.back: Keep the lift small, and keep your back still.
a4.back-leg.done: And rest that leg. Nicely done.
a4.knee-curl.intro: Knee curl. For lifting your feet over steps and curbs.
a4.knee-curl.demo.1: Bend one knee and bring your heel up behind you.
a4.knee-curl.breath: Breathe out as your heel comes up, breathe in as it lowers.
a4.knee-curl.easier: Easier: bring your heel up only a little way.
a4.knee-curl.form.1: Keep your knees side by side. Only the lower leg moves.
a4.knee-curl.form.2: Keep your other knee soft, and your body tall.
a4.knee-curl.harder: Want more? Loosen your grip, hands just resting on the chair.
a4.knee-curl.var.joint: Bend only as far as feels comfortable for your knee.
a4.knee-curl.done: Set your foot down softly. Lovely work.
a4.mini-squat.intro: Mini-squat. For sitting down gently and getting back up.
a4.mini-squat.setup.1: Both hands on the chair back, feet hip-width apart.
a4.mini-squat.demo.1: A small bend of the knees, as if you're about to sit.
a4.mini-squat.breath: Breathe in as you bend, breathe out as you stand up.
a4.mini-squat.easier: Easier: just a tiny bend. That still counts.
a4.mini-squat.form.1: Sit back a little. Your knees stay over your feet.
a4.mini-squat.form.2: Heels stay down. Back straight, chest up.
a4.mini-squat.harder: Want more? Go down more slowly, still only halfway.
a4.mini-squat.var.knees.1: Only go halfway. If your heels start to lift, come back up.
a4.mini-squat.var.knees.2: Keep your knees in line with your toes. Don't let them cave in.
a4.mini-squat.done: Stand tall, knees soft. Well done.
a4.arm-raise.intro: Arm raises. For lifting bags onto the counter.
a4.arm-raise.setup.1: Sit tall, feet flat, hands resting on your thighs.
a4.arm-raise.demo.1: Arms rise in front of you, up to shoulder height, then slowly down.
a4.arm-raise.demo.2: Now out to the sides, also to shoulder height.
a4.arm-raise.breath: Breathe out as your arms rise, breathe in as they lower.
a4.arm-raise.easier: Easier: lift only partway, below your shoulders.
a4.arm-raise.form.2: Shoulders stay low, away from your ears.
a4.arm-raise.harder: Want more? Pause at the top for a moment.
a4.arm-raise.var.shoulder: Stop at shoulder height or lower, wherever feels comfortable.
a4.arm-raise.done: Rest your hands on your thighs. Nicely done.
a4.row.intro: Seated row. For pulling open heavy doors and drawers.
a4.row.setup.1: Sit tall, away from the back of your chair, feet flat.
a4.row.setup.2: No band needed. Imagine you're pulling a rope toward you.
a4.row.demo.1: Arms reach forward, then elbows pull straight back.
a4.row.breath: Breathe out as you pull back, breathe in as you reach forward.
a4.row.easier: Easier: a smaller pull. Bring your elbows back just a little.
a4.row.form.1: Squeeze your shoulder blades together, gently.
a4.row.form.2: Elbows close to your sides. Chin level.
a4.row.harder: Want more? Hold the squeeze for a count of two.
a10.open.1: Time for a gentle stretch. Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat on the floor.
a10.open.2: We'll move slowly and breathe. Stretch to a gentle pull, never to pain.
a10.open.stand: Stand behind your chair and hold the back with both hands. Feet about hip-width apart.
a10.cool.open: Lovely walking. Stay seated, and let's cool down with a few easy stretches.
a10.into.2: Go only as far as feels comfortable.
a10.hold.1: Breathe in through your nose… and out through your mouth.
a10.hold.2: Breathe into it. Let your shoulders stay soft.
a10.hold.3: A gentle pull is enough. No bouncing.
a10.hold.4: Keep breathing. There's no need to push.
a10.hold.5: If it pinches or hurts, ease off a little.
a10.switch.2: Come back to the middle… and now the other side.
a10.easier: Here's an easier way. Smaller and slower is just as good.
a10.close.1: That's your stretch for today. Take one more slow breath.
a10.close.2: Nice and easy. You gave your body some care today.
a10.cool.close: All done. Sit for a moment, and have a sip of water.
a10.neck-turn.intro: Neck turns. They make it easier to look over your shoulder.
a10.neck-turn.setup: Sit tall, shoulders down, and look straight ahead.
a10.neck-turn.move: Slowly turn your head toward your shoulder, as far as is comfortable.
a10.neck-turn.easy: Just turn halfway, nice and slow, and keep your eyes open.
a10.neck-tilt.intro: Now the side of your neck.
a10.neck-tilt.setup: Rest your right hand on your left shoulder, and let that shoulder stay low.
a10.neck-tilt.move: Slowly tilt your head to the right, ear toward your shoulder. No pulling.
a10.neck-tilt.easy: Skip the hand, and just tilt your head a little.
a10.chest.intro: Chest and shoulders. Good for sitting tall.
a10.chest.setup: Sit forward, away from the back of your chair.
a10.chest.move: Draw your shoulders back and down. Open your arms to the sides, and lift your chest gently.
a10.chest.easy: Rest your hands on your hips, and just draw your shoulders back.
a10.twist.intro: Upper back twist. It helps with turning to reach for things.
a10.twist.setup: Cross your arms and rest your hands on your shoulders. Feet flat.
a10.twist.move: Turn your upper body to one side. Your hips stay still, your head turns with you.
a10.twist.easy: Turn just a small way. That's plenty.
a10.side.setup: Sit tall with your feet flat and a little apart.
a10.side.move: Reach one arm up and over your head, and lean gently to the other side.
a10.side.easy: Keep your arm by your side, and just lean a little.
a10.thigh.intro: The back of your thigh. It makes bending down a little easier.
a10.thigh.setup: Sit near the front of your chair. Stretch one leg out, heel on the floor, toes pointing up.
a10.thigh.move: Rest your hands on your other leg. Lean forward from your hips, and keep your back long.
a10.thigh.easy: Keep that knee a little bent, and lean forward only a little.
a10.ankle.setup: Hold the side of your seat, and lift one foot just off the floor.
a10.ankle.move: Point your toes away from you… then bring them back toward you. Slow and smooth.
a10.ankle.easy: Keep your heel on the floor, and just lift and lower your toes.
a10.calf.intro: Calf stretch. Hold on to your chair the whole time.
a10.calf.setup: Hands on the back of your chair. Step one foot back, and keep both feet flat.
a10.calf.move: Bend your front knee a little, keep the back leg straight and the heel down. You'll feel it in your calf.
a10.calf.easy: Take a shorter step back, and let your back knee bend a little.
a10.chin-tuck.intro: Chin tuck. A small, gentle move for your neck.
a10.chin-tuck.setup: Sit tall and look straight ahead. Eyes stay level, and never tip your head back.
a10.chin-tuck.move: Glide your head straight back, like a gentle double chin… then let it go.
a10.chin-tuck.easy: Make the glide smaller. A tiny movement is plenty.
a10.shoulder-roll.intro: Shoulder rolls. A nice way to loosen up your shoulders.
a10.shoulder-roll.setup: Sit tall, with your hands resting on your thighs.
a10.shoulder-roll.move: Roll your shoulders up, back, and down, in one slow circle.
a10.shoulder-roll.easy: Make the circles smaller, and keep them slow.
a10.upper-back.intro: Upper back reach. You'll feel it between your shoulder blades.
a10.upper-back.setup: Sit tall. Bring both arms forward at shoulder height, palms facing away.
a10.upper-back.move: Reach your hands forward, and let your upper back round a little. Your lower back stays tall.
a10.upper-back.easy: Keep your whole back tall, and just reach your arms. Hands a little lower is fine.
a10.overhead.intro: Overhead reach at the wall. It helps with reaching a high cupboard.
a10.overhead.setup: Stand facing the wall, close enough to rest your palms on it at shoulder height.
a10.overhead.move: Slowly walk your hands up the wall, as high as is comfortable. Keep your heels down, and don't arch your back.
a10.overhead.easy: Only reach up to eye level. That's plenty.
a10.overhead.seated: Stay in your chair instead. Sit tall, and slowly reach both arms up in front of you.
a10.thigh.back: Just stretch the leg out and sit tall. No need to lean forward.
a10.warm.1: Let's warm up first. Easy marching, and let your arms swing.
a10.warm.end: Nice and warm. Now let's start stretching.
a10.hold.start.2: Stay right there. Nice, slow breaths.
a10.round2.1: Once more. It may feel a little easier to settle in.
a10.round2.2: Let's go back into that one. Ease in, a little at a time.
a10.reps: Slow and gentle. I'll count for you.
a10.to-wall: Let go of the chair when you feel steady, and walk over to a wall.
a10.to-sit: Now come and sit down. Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat.
a10.cool.open.stand: Lovely walking. Stay close to your chair, and let's cool down with a few easy stretches.
a10.breathe.open: Let's finish with some slow breathing. Sit back in your chair, feet flat.
a10.breathe.how: Breathe in through your nose for a count of five. Then out through your mouth for five.
a10.breathe.in: In through your nose… two… three… four… five.
a10.breathe.out: And out through your mouth… two… three… four… five.
a10.breathe.mid: Gentle breaths. There's no need to force them.
a10.breathe.end: Let your breathing go back to its own easy pace.
a11.extra.note: This one is a little extra. Today's session is still there whenever you're ready.
a11.balance.place: Set your chair with its back against a wall, or use a kitchen counter.
a11.balance.reach: Keep the chair or counter within reach the whole time.
a11.balance.posture: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, knees soft.
a11.balance.shift: Now shift your weight gently onto one foot… then over to the other.
a11.hands.two: Hold on with both hands for this one.
a11.hands.one: Hold on with one hand, and keep the other close by.
a11.hands.tips: Just your fingertips on the chair, if you feel steady.
a11.hands.keep: Keep at least one hand on the chair the whole time.
a11.hands.back: Both hands back on the chair, and take a breath.
a11.sts.intro: Now have a seat for sit-to-stand.
a11.sts.two: Push up with both hands on the seat. Stand tall, then pause for a breath.
a11.sts.one: Feeling steady? This time, push up with just one hand.
a11.tandem.intro: Tandem stance. Stand behind your chair, feet side by side.
a11.tandem.move: Place one foot right in front of the other, heel touching your toes.
a11.tandem.easy: Wobbly? Set your front foot a little to the side. That still counts.
a11.tandem.jr: Keep your feet in line. Never cross one over the other.
a11.tandem.switch: Step back to the start. Now the other foot in front.
a11.single-leg.intro: Single-leg stand. Feet side by side, close to your chair.
a11.side-walk.intro: Sideways walking. Face your kitchen counter, and rest your hands on it.
a11.side-walk.move: Step one foot out to the side, then bring the other to meet it.
a11.side-walk.count: Ten steps this way, then ten steps back.
a11.side-walk.nocounter: No counter? Stay by your chair, and step out and back in place.
a11.side-walk.easy: Keep your steps small, and slide your hands along as you go.
a11.heel-toe.intro: Heel and toe raises, standing. Hold the back of your chair.
a11.heel-toe.up: Rise up onto your toes… and lower your heels slowly.
a11.heel-toe-walk.intro: Heel-to-toe walk. Stand beside a wall, fingertips resting on it.
a11.heel-toe-walk.move: Step one foot right in front of the other, heel to toes. One slow step at a time.
a11.heel-toe-walk.easy: Leave a small gap between your feet if you need it.
a11.balance.sit: Now sit down in your chair, and let your feet rest.
a11.balance.close: That's balance done for today. Nice and steady.
a11.morning.open: Good morning. Let's wake up your body gently, right in your chair.
a11.morning.sit: Sit tall, feet flat, and take three slow breaths.
a11.morning.dizzy: Feeling lightheaded? Stay seated, and rest as long as you need.
a11.morning.gentle: Your muscles are still waking up, so we'll keep every move small and slow.
a11.neck-turn.reps: Turn your head slowly to one side, back to the middle, then the other.
a11.twist.reps: Turn a small way to one side, back to the middle, then the other side.
a11.march.seated: Now easy marching in your chair. Lift one knee, then the other.
a11.ankle.circles: Now slow circles with your toes, one way… then the other way.
a11.morning.stand: Last one: sit-to-stand. We'll do three, slowly, pushing up with both hands.
a11.morning.lightheaded: If you feel lightheaded when you stand, sit back down. That's fine.
a11.morning.still: Stand still for three slow breaths. Hold the chair if you like.
a11.morning.close: That's your morning stretch. Have a lovely day.
a11.break.open.1: Commercial break walk. Let's use the break to get your feet moving.
a11.break.open.2: Sit or stand by your chair, whichever feels right today.
a11.break.mid: Keep half an ear on your show. You can pause anytime.
a11.break.close.1: That's your break walk. Enjoy the rest of your show.
a11.break.close.2: Nicely done. A few minutes of moving, right in the middle of your day.
a11.wind.open: Time to wind down. Sit back in your chair, and let it hold you.
a11.wind.setup: Feet flat, about hip-width apart. Let your hands rest in your lap.
a11.wind.screen: You can set your phone down. There's nothing you need to watch.
a11.wind.stretch: First, a few slow stretches for your neck and chest.
a11.wind.breathe: Now we'll simply breathe together for a few minutes.
a11.wind.mid.1: If your mind wanders, that's fine. Come back to the count.
a11.wind.mid.2: Let your jaw soften, and let your shoulders drop.
a11.wind.mid.3: With each breath out, let a little more of the day go.
a11.wind.close: That's all for tonight. Rest well.
a11.posture.open: A quick reset for when you've been sitting a while.
a11.posture.setup: Sit toward the front of your chair, and let's open up a little.
a11.posture.to-wall: Last one at the wall. Stand up slowly, take a breath, then walk over.
a11.posture.close: That's your reset. Notice how your shoulders feel, then carry on with your day.
a11.steady.open: Two more minutes now, for steadier feet. Stand behind your chair.
a11.steady.seated: Two more minutes now, right in your chair, for steadier feet.
a11.recover: If you wobble, a quick step to catch yourself is fine. That's part of the practice.
a4.v1.rest: Sit and rest for a minute. Breathe easy, and sip some water if you like.
a4.v1.set2: Second set now. Same as before, slow and steady.
a11.back-ext.intro: Standing back extension. Stand tall, hands on your hips.
a11.back-ext.move: Lean back just a little, chin level, eyes ahead… then come back up tall.
a11.back-ext.small: Only a small lean. You should feel your chest lift, not your neck.
a11.back-walk.intro: Walking backwards. Stand at your kitchen counter, hands resting on it.
a11.back-walk.move: Step back slowly, toes first, then the heel. Keep looking ahead.
a11.back-walk.count: Ten small steps back, then ten steps forward.
a11.back-walk.easy: Keep your steps small, and slide your hands along the counter.
a11.walk-turn.intro: Walk and turn. Start at one end of your kitchen counter.
a11.walk-turn.move: Walk four steps along it, then turn around slowly, in small steps.
a11.walk-turn.back: Now walk back, and turn again at the start.
a11.walk-turn.easy: Take the turn in tiny steps, and keep a hand on the counter.
a11.heel-walk.intro: Heel and toe walking. Stand at your counter, one hand resting on it.
a11.heel-walk.heels: Lift your toes, and take ten small steps on your heels.
a11.heel-walk.toes: Now rise onto your toes, and take ten small steps back.
a11.heel-walk.easy: Too much? Do the raises standing still instead. That still counts.
a11.ladder.one: Last time you were steady with both hands. Try one hand today, if it feels right.
a11.ladder.tips: Last time one hand felt steady. Try just your fingertips today, if it feels right.
a11.ladder.down: Let's keep both hands on today. That's a smart choice.
a12.check.setup: Sit near the front of your chair, feet flat. Ready?
a12.check.go: Go. Stand up all the way, then sit back down. At your own pace.
a12.check.stop: And stop. Rest a moment, then enter how many times you stood up.
